observation.transcript:
AI Mode Conversation
You said: operational semiotics

Operational semiotics is Charls Pearson's formal research program that breaks down natural-language sentences into mood and semantic operators to analyze transformations of sign structures. [1, 2]
Core Concepts
* Theory of Operational Semiotics (TOS): Developed primarily between 1982 and 1998, it models how meaning works by applying explicit formal operators rather than relying solely on traditional syntax-semantics-pragmatics categories. [1, 2]
* Operator Breakdown: Sentences are factored into mood operators and semantic operators—including intent-based "Words to World" operators—to map out underlying sign dynamics. [1]
* Boundary of Description: It stops formal description once the internal sign transformation has been mathematically or logically specified. [1]
Distinction from Operative Semiotics
* Operational vs. Operative: They are distinct research programs and not interchangeable spelling variants.
* Operational Semiotics: Focuses strictly on specifying formal operator transformations within sign structures.
* Operative Semiotics: Follows sign transformations further out into executing substrates, institutional frameworks, labor costs, and distributive consequences in the real world. [1, 2]
Would you like to explore how operational semiotics breaks down specific natural language sentences or look closer at its relationship to computational information systems?
